newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Fifty firms interested in Brazil Petrobras deals.
newsitem.headline: Fifty firms interested in Brazil Petrobras deals.

text.p: More than 50 oil companies have obtained confidential information on 149 oil exploration and production projects Brazil's state oil monopoly Petrobras wants to pursue with other firms once the oil sector is opened to private competition, the O Estado de Sao Paulo newspaper said Sunday.
The companies who applied to see the project information had to sign an agreement of confidentiality, O Estado said.
The 149 projects identified by Petrobras require investments between $5 million and $900 million, it said.

A bill regulating the opening of the oil industry is currently being considered in Congress. It provides for the creation of a regulatory body, the National Petroleum Agency (ANP), which would approve licenses for exploration and production concessions.

"Once the legislation is approved and the ANP has been created Petrobras will be ready to establish partnerships," a spokesman for Petrobras' exploration and production department was quoted as saying by O Estado de Sao Paulo.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
